overview.summary: Fizz Buzz is a number-printing program that iterates through a sequence of integers and replaces specific multiples with designated words. It is a foundational programming exercise used to validate basic control flow, modulo arithmetic, and output formatting skills.
goals: Provide a correct, deterministic output for any given input range
Demonstrate clear branching logic for multiple divisibility conditions
Produce human-readable output suitable for display or logging

in_scope: Iterating over a consecutive range of positive integers
Replacing multiples of both 3 and 5 with 'FizzBuzz'

functional_requirements.description: The program shall accept a start and end integer defining an inclusive range to iterate over.
For each integer in the range, if it is divisible by both 3 and 5, the program shall output 'FizzBuzz'.
For each integer in the range, if it is divisible by 3 only, the program shall output 'Fizz'.
For each integer in the range, if it is divisible by 5 only, the program shall output 'Buzz'.
For each integer in the range that meets none of the above conditions, the program shall output the integer itself.
Each output value shall appear on its own line.
The divisibility check for both 3 and 5 (FR-02) shall be evaluated before the individual checks (FR-03, FR-04) to ensure correct output precedence.

non_functional_requirements.description: The program shall produce output in O(n) time relative to the size of the input range.
The program shall produce identical output for the same input range on every execution (deterministic).
The program shall handle a range of at least 1 to 1,000,000 without error or performance degradation.

acceptance_criteria.scenario: Single value divisible by both 3 and 5 (e.g. 15)
Single value not divisible by 3 or 5 (e.g. 1)
